answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a VDF chain of sequential modular squarings, where every step depends on the previous result. GPUs can accelerate individual operations, but cannot parallelize one chain or erase its elapsed-time cost; simulating many clones requires separate chains and proportionally more work. A Wesolowski proof lets a verifier check completion efficiently, while vault, ripple, and summit serve only as labels, not shortcuts around the delay.
